people.name: Novatian
people.summary: Leading Roman presbyter and the first Roman theologian to write in Latin (De Trinitate), Novatian ran the Roman church's correspondence during the vacancy of 250-251. Defeated by Cornelius in the episcopal election, he was consecrated rival bishop by rigorists who refused readmission to the lapsed, founding the Novatianist church, which survived in Constantinople and Phrygia into the fifth century. Tradition makes him a martyr under Valerian.

people.name: Kartir
people.summary: Zoroastrian priest who rose under Shapur I to become, under Bahram I and Bahram II, the most powerful religious figure of the Sasanian state; his four inscriptions (Naqsh-e Rostam, Naqsh-e Rajab, Sar Mashhad and the Ka'ba-ye Zartosht) boast of founding fire temples and persecuting Jews, Buddhists, Brahmins, Nazarenes, Christians, Baptists and Manichaeans, and he engineered the death of Mani (276/7).

people.name: Tertullian
people.summary: Carthaginian rhetorician and the first major Christian writer in Latin, Tertullian addressed the Apologeticum (197) to provincial governors, coined the Latin theological terms trinitas and persona, wrote against Marcion and Praxeas, on the spectacles, idolatry and the soldier's crown, and later joined the rigorist New Prophecy (Montanism). His "the blood of Christians is seed" and "what has Athens to do with Jerusalem?" became proverbial.

people.name: Gregory Thaumaturgus
people.summary: Born Theodore to a pagan family of Neocaesarea in Pontus, he studied law and then philosophy under Origen at Caesarea, whose method he describes in a farewell Panegyric. As bishop of Neocaesarea (c. 240-270) he converted much of Pontus, reputedly finding 17 Christians and leaving 17 pagans; his Canonical Letter deals with Christians who collaborated with Gothic raiders c. 254.

people.name: Methodius of Olympus
people.summary: Bishop in Lycia (Olympus) and author of the Symposium of the Ten Virgins, a Christian imitation of Plato praising virginity, and of treatises against Origen's views on the resurrection and against Porphyry; tradition, doubted by some, makes him a martyr in 311.

people.name: Eunomius
people.summary: Cappadocian secretary and disciple of Aetius, briefly bishop of Cyzicus (360), Eunomius systematised the Anomoean doctrine that God's essence is "unbegottenness" and can be known, so that the begotten Son cannot share it; refuted at length by Basil and Gregory of Nyssa, he was exiled repeatedly and his followers, the Eunomians, survived as a sect.

people.name: Petronius Probus
people.summary: Head of the Anician clan and the richest man of the west, Probus held four praetorian prefectures (Illyricum 364, Gaul, Italy-Illyricum-Africa 368-375 and 383) and the consulship of 371. Ammianus portrays him as greedy and fearful, "like a fish out of water" out of office; he patronised the young Ambrose, sending him to govern Aemilia-Liguria with the words "act not as a judge but as a bishop". His Christian epitaph and sarcophagus stood behind St Peter's.
